verses.text: As they came near Jerusalem—at Bethphage and Bethany, by the Mount of Olives—Jesus sent two of his disciples ahead
and said, “Go into the village in front of you. As soon as you enter, you’ll find a young donkey tied up, one nobody has ridden. Untie it and bring it here.
“If anyone asks, ‘Why are you doing that?’ say, ‘The Lord needs it, and he’ll send it right back.’”
They went and found a young donkey tied outside by a doorway, out on the street. They untied it.
Some people standing there asked, “Hey, why are you untying that young donkey?”
They answered just as Jesus had told them, and the people let them take it.
They brought the donkey to Jesus, threw their garments over it, and he sat on it.
Many people spread their garments on the road, while others cut leafy branches from the fields and laid them down too.
People walking ahead of him and those following shouted, “Hosanna! Blessed is the one coming in the Lord’s name!
“Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!”
Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple. He looked around at everything, but since it was already evening, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.
The next day, as they were leaving Bethany, Jesus was hungry.
From a distance he saw a fig tree with leaves and went over to see if it had any fruit. But when he got there, he found nothing but leaves—it wasn’t fig season.
Jesus said to the tree, “May nobody ever eat fruit from you again!” His disciples heard him.
They came to Jerusalem. Jesus entered the temple and began driving out the people buying and selling there. He flipped the money changers’ tables and the seats of those selling doves.
He wouldn’t let anyone carry anything through the temple.
He taught them: “Isn’t it written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations’? But you’ve turned it into a hideout for robbers!”
The chief priests and legal teachers heard this and started looking for a way to kill Jesus. They feared him because the whole crowd was amazed at his teaching.
When evening came, Jesus and his disciples left the city.
The next morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots.
Peter remembered and said, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree you cursed has dried up.”
Jesus answered, “Have faith in God.
“I’m telling you the truth: if someone tells this mountain, ‘Get up and throw yourself into the sea,’ and doesn’t doubt inside but believes it will happen, it will happen.
“So I tell you: whatever you pray and ask for, believe you’ve received it, and it will be yours.
“Whenever you stand praying, forgive anyone you’re holding something against, so your Father in heaven can forgive your wrongs too.
“But if you don’t forgive others, your Father in heaven won’t forgive your wrongs either.”
They came to Jerusalem again. While Jesus was walking in the temple, the chief priests, legal teachers, and elders approached him
and asked, “What authority do you have to do these things? Who gave you the right?”
Jesus said, “I’ll ask you one question. Answer me, and then I’ll tell you what authority I have to do these things.
“John’s baptism—was it from heaven or from people? Answer me.”
They discussed it among themselves: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he’ll ask, ‘Then why didn’t you believe him?’
“But if we say, ‘From people’…” They were afraid of the crowd, because everyone considered John a real prophet.
So they answered Jesus, “We don’t know.” Jesus said, “Then I won’t tell you what authority I have to do these things either.”
